benchmark_kind: the real MetaQA federated split, tested against both premises the design rests on
scope_warning: Computed from the actual federated party data the recorded runs used. Degree and volume figures are measurements. No MPC was run; the consequences for each mechanism follow from its cost model.

per_owner.note: party_1's max source degree of 2,089 matches the lossless_max_source_degree already recorded in relation_page_cost_model.json, which cross-checks that this is the same data the earlier planning used.

premise_1_relation_narrowing.claim_the_design_rests_on: max source degree is much larger than max (source, relation) degree, so keying by (source, relation) narrows the bucket
premise_1_relation_narrowing.verdict: FALSE on this data, per owner as well as federation-wide. The relation-paged layout provides no narrowing on MetaQA. See metaqa_real_degree_profile.json for the cause: hub sources are attribute nodes reached by inverse edges, whose edges all sit under one relation.

premise_2_unequal_owner_volumes.claim_the_design_rests_on: owners hold very different amounts of data, so publishing B_i leaks something sensitive and uniform padding taxes small participants heavily
premise_2_unequal_owner_volumes.verdict: ABSENT under the BUNDLED split, which is a random 50/50 edge partition and the least realistic federation available. Not absent from MetaQA: splitting by relation type, by subject entity, or into one large archive plus small contributors gives 1.83x to 2.02x skew from the same graph. See the CORRECTION field and volume_hiding_on_real_federation.json.
premise_2_unequal_owner_volumes.why: The available split appears to be a roughly even partition of one knowledge graph, not a federation of institutions of differing sizes. The motivating scenario -- one large hospital and twenty small clinics -- is not what this data represents.

combined_reading: The relation-narrowing premise is false on MetaQA structurally. The unequal-volume premise is absent only because of how this project split the graph, and is restored by any realistic federation model. The implementations are correct throughout; what was wrong was assuming both properties held.
what_survives_unaffected: The measurement study: the 261x threat-model premium, the layout-versus-micro-optimisation ablation, and the negative results on DORAM, sorting, and batching.
metaqa_real_lossiness.json: the supported packed scan discards 56.8% of MetaQA at fanout 2. The lossiness problem is real and remains unsolved.
Federation-wide frontier compaction and packed descriptors, which depend on owner count rather than on either premise.
Contribution hiding (Definition 1), which is about per-query match counts and is independent of both premises.
what_this_means_for_a_writeup: Neither the 17.5x crossover nor the volume-hiding motivation may be presented as MetaQA results. Both need either a dataset exhibiting the relevant property, with that property stated and measured, or reframing as what they are: mechanisms characterised on synthetic distributions, with the real dataset reported as a negative case.
what_this_does_not_show: That no real federation has these properties; only that this one does not.
Any executed MetaQA run of the relation-paged backend, which has still never been performed.
That the mechanisms are incorrect; correctness is established separately and is unaffected.

CORRECTION.what_was_overstated: This file originally read as though MetaQA is a poor fit for the project. That is too broad and conflates two different things.

what_is_actually_true.simgrag_use_of_metaqa: SimGRAG used MetaQA as a SINGLE knowledge graph for graph-RAG, which is entirely appropriate; MetaQA is a standard KGQA benchmark. Nothing here argues against that, and SimGRAG is not a federated system.
what_is_actually_true.premise_1_narrowing: Still FALSE and not recoverable by re-splitting. The hubs are attribute nodes reached by inverse edges whose degree sits under a single relation, which is inherent to the graph. Forward-only edges give 2.83x, and hub filtering is a standard KGQA practice; either response needs stating and measuring.
what_is_actually_true.premise_2_volume_skew: RECOVERABLE, and the original verdict here was wrong to imply otherwise. The 1.003 skew is a property of the SPLIT, not of MetaQA. The bundled split is a random 50/50 partition of edges -- 61% of sources appear in both parties with the same relations -- which is the least realistic federation obtainable. Realistic splits of the same data give 1.83x to 2.02x skew; see volume_hiding_on_real_federation.json.

CORRECTION.revised_verdict: One premise fails structurally on MetaQA and one fails only under the bundled split. The volume-hiding mechanism has a defensible real-data case once the federation is modelled rather than randomly partitioned; the relation-paged layout does not.
